newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH BONDS STUCK IN OVERSEAS TREND, GAP STEADY.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH BONDS STUCK IN OVERSEAS TREND, GAP STEADY.

text.p: Finnish bonds on Thursday
remained at earlier lower levels after U.S. treasuries dragged
German Bunds down, but the benchmark yield gap over Germany was
flat at 28 basis points.
Dealers said the mood was nervous but the short-term outlook
still stable. "Sentiment is nervous, but I think the (yield)
spread over Germany will not move much," one dealer said.
The markka was moving in a narrow range below 3.02 per mark,
and one dealer said domestic demand was offset by foreign
interest in reducing and closing positions taken early in the
year.
In January, DEM/FIM moved quickly towards 2.92 from about
3.00 with some international players said buying markka for
speculative gains: some operators estimated about 30 to 40
billion markka worth of funds flowed in.
The Bank of Finland responded by allowing the government to
buy its currency directly from the market, which stopped the
markka strengthening, sending DEM/FIM higher.
"Based on domestic interests only, DEM/FIM would now be
trading 2.9850-2.9959," a forex dealer said, adding that foreign
interest to buy marks for markka was seen near 3.00.
